questions.question: A function has defers, and one panics — what's the execution order?
questions.title: Defer Ordering Scenario
questions.direct_answer: Panic starts unwinding: defers run LIFO (last first). If a defer calls recover, unwinding stops and the function returns normally. The recover must be in a defer, and in the SAME goroutine.

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    P[panic boom] --> D3[defer 3: recover wrapper runs FIRST]
    D3 --> REC[recover called — unwind stops]
    REC --> D2[defer 2 runs — normal return path]
    D2 --> D1[defer 1 runs]
    D1 --> RET[function returns normally]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The defer stack and panic's interaction, mechanically: defers are a linked list per goroutine (g._defer). Panic walks this list — calling each deferred function and popping it. A defer that calls recover() sets the panicking flag to recovered — subsequent unwinding stops; the function returns normally. The remaining defers (already-popped-to but not yet run) execute as part of that normal return.

The recover-goroutine constraint: panic and recover are per-goroutine — the defer that recovers must be on the panicking goroutine. A helper goroutine cannot recover the main goroutine's panic; an unrecovered panic in ANY goroutine crashes the program.

The real-world pattern (where this scenario lives): an HTTP handler defer-recovers, converts to a 500, and logs the stack — each goroutine (each request) has its own boundary. The server survives per-request panics because of this exact ordering.
